AI Overview
City Brawl most commonly refers to a few different action and fighting games, including a web-based physics brawler, a retro-style side-scrolling beat 'em up, and a 3D mech combat title:
1. City Brawl (Web/Browser Game)
Genre: Physics-based street brawler
Developer: AzGames
Platform: Web browsers (PC and mobile)
Gameplay: You control a street fighter battling waves of gangs and bosses across urban levels. You collect oranges as currency to upgrade your fighter's punch power, kick power, health, and weapon techniques. You can play it directly via City Brawl. 
2. Fallen City Brawl
Genre: Retro-inspired side-scrolling beat 'em up (channeling late '80s and '90s arcade classics)
Platform: PlayStation 5 and other modern systems
Gameplay: You choose from four unique characters (plus a companion wolf) to fight through seven stages of pixel-art urban action. It features deep combo systems, parries, weapons (like bats, pipes, and chainsaws), and local co-op. You can view details on the PlayStation Store. 
3. Override: Mech City Brawl
Genre: 3D mech-based fighting game
Platform: PC, PlayStation 4, and other platforms
Gameplay: You pilot skyscraper-sized mechs in 3D arenas modeled after real-world cities (like Tokyo and San Francisco). It supports one-on-one fights, local/online party co-op, and a single-player campaign.
